_README: MANUALLY CURATED from official Rutgers catalog prose. This is a DERIVATION,
not a machine extraction: Rutgers publishes the CS major requirements as an
English paragraph, not as structured data. Every node below carries the
sentence it came from so the derivation can be re-checked against the source.
KNOWN GAP: the prose says electives come 'from a designated list of courses
in computer science and related disciplines ... For details, see a computer
science adviser or the departmental website.' That designated list is NOT
published in the catalog. Only the constraints the prose states directly are
encoded here; the non-CS elective options are deliberately absent rather

program_version.source_prose: The B.A. option requires 51-55 credits (depending on 3-credit or 4-credit elective options); the B.S. option requires 67-72 credits.

requirements.name: Computer Science B.A. Major
requirements.source_prose: The basic major, leading to a bachelor of arts (B.A.) degree, consists of: 1) six required courses in computer science, 01:198:111, 112, 205, 206, 211, and 344; 2) three courses in mathematics, 01:640:151-152 and 01:640:250; and 3) five electives from a designated list of courses in computer science and related disciplines.

requirements.name: Required Computer Science Courses
requirements.source_prose: six required courses in computer science, 01:198:111, 112, 205, 206, 211, and 344

requirements.name: Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms
Computer Science Electives
requirements.notes: The catalog defers the designated elective list to the department; only CS courses at the 300 level or above are encoded here, which the prose supports directly. Non-CS elective options are NOT encoded because the catalog does not publish them.
requirements.source_prose: five electives from a designated list of courses in computer science and related disciplines (e.g., electrical engineering, mathematics). At most, two of the five electives may be taken outside the Department of Computer Science; at least two must be computer science courses at the 300 level or above.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: At most two of the five electives may be taken outside the Department of Computer Science; at least two must be CS at the 300 level or above.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: IMPLEMENTED as group constraints on CS_ELECTIVES (max_outside_subject / min_at_level), not as a program rule.

program_rules.name: At most one grade of D in required major courses
program_rules.source_prose: No more than one grade of D can be accepted in the courses required for the major.

program_rules.name: Courses that earn no credit for declared CS majors
program_rules.source_prose: Declared computer science majors (198) will not receive credit (major or degree) for subsequent enrollment in computer science 105, 107,110, 142, 170, or 405.

program_rules.name: Minimum seven courses in the Rutgers-New Brunswick CS department
program_rules.not_evaluable_reason: The rule requires knowing which courses were taken AT Rutgers-New Brunswick. StudentCourse records no transfer provenance, and a cross-listed course carries another department's code, so the count cannot be computed without guessing. Rutgers publishes no transfer-equivalence rule we could apply here.
program_rules.source_prose: A minimum of seven courses must be taken in the Rutgers University-New Brunswick Department of Computer Science.
